The evidence is enough to fix this. Some customers migrated to the new CRM carry numeric region codes ('01'–'04') instead of region names. raw_region_map is the mapping the CRM note points to: 01→WEST, 02→EAST, 03→NORTH, 04→SOUTH.

The map has exactly four rows with distinct codes, so a left join on the code cannot duplicate customer rows. The fix is to map the code to its name where one matches and otherwise keep the existing upper-cased region name. The output columns stay the same. I considered whether the mapping might be ambiguous, but the map table is explicit and the note documents it.

Whitespace in the codes is not a concern: the profile shows exactly '01' through '04'. I will trim the value before joining anyway.

The gold_region_daily step reads silver_customers, so it will pick up the corrected regions on re-run without any change.

```json
{"diagnosis": "Customers migrated to the new CRM have numeric region codes (01-04) instead of region names; raw_region_map provides the code-to-name mapping, but silver_customers does not apply it, so gold_region_daily has wrong region groups.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_customers": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_customers AS SELECT c.customer_id, COALESCE(upper(m.region_name), upper(c.region)) AS region FROM raw_customers c LEFT JOIN raw_region_map m ON trim(c.region) = m.region_code"}}
```
